questions.q:
A project team is conducting a needs analysis for a design project.

During the needs analysis, the team will
options: identify opportunities.
develop financial plans.
formulate a time and action plan.
establish criteria for material selection.
questions.explanation: A needs analysis is a questioning exercise that explores the problem and identifies the needs and opportunities to be met. Financial plans, time and action plans, and material-selection criteria are developed later, once the need has been clarified.

questions.q:
A furniture designer is to develop a cabinet.

Which factor should be considered first?
options: The tools available
The needs of the client
The time frame of the project
The selling price of the cabinet
questions.explanation: Every project begins with the need: the designer must first establish what the client requires, through a needs analysis, before tools, scheduling or cost can be meaningfully addressed. Those other factors are constraints that follow once the need is defined.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of conducting market research prior to product development?
options: To formulate finance and action plans
To determine suitable advertising methods
To identify the needs and wants of the target audience
To determine the values and beliefs of various cultural groups
questions.explanation: Market research carried out before development is how you confirm a need is genuine: it identifies the needs and wants of the target audience so the product is appropriate for them. Finance plans and advertising decisions come later in the process.

questions.q: Why do designers establish and review 'criteria to evaluate success' when designing?
options: To increase the number of sales of a product
To ensure environmental factors are considered
To ensure the final design meets the specified needs
To maintain product awareness for further refinement of innovative products
questions.explanation: Criteria to evaluate success are the measurable standards set in the proposal and checked against the finished project, so they exist to ensure the final design meets the specified needs. This is the proposal-to-evaluation bookend. The other options are narrower commercial or environmental concerns.

questions.q: A major design project proposal must outline three things. Which option correctly lists them?
options: The need, the budget, and the time and action plan
The identification and exploration of the need, the areas of investigation, and the criteria to evaluate success
The solution, the materials, and the manufacturing process
The market research, the prototype, and the final evaluation
questions.explanation: The syllabus is precise: the proposal outlines the identification and exploration of the need, the areas of investigation, and the criteria to evaluate success — remembered as NICe. The most commonly forgotten part is the areas of investigation, the map of the research to come.

questions.q: In the episode's terms, what is a 'niche'?
options: A consumer-driven problem experienced by a large, mainstream target market
A small, specialised group of consumers for whom no adequate product currently exists
The set of measurable standards a finished project must meet
A questioning exercise used to clarify and define the design task
questions.explanation: A niche is a special case of an opportunity: a small, specialised group of consumers for whom no adequate product currently exists. Finding a genuine niche, an unmet specialised market, makes a strong MDP.

questions.q: From memory: what three things must a major design project proposal contain?
keyPoints: N — the identification and exploration of the Need, stated clearly and evidenced by the needs analysis and research.
I — the areas of Investigation: what you'll research to solve it (materials, existing products, users, techniques).
C — the measurable Criteria to evaluate success, both functional and aesthetic.
Anchor with the mnemonic NICe; the most commonly forgotten part is the areas of Investigation.
questions.explanation: If you recalled all three parts of NICe, grade Good or Easy. If you missed the areas of investigation, the most commonly forgotten one, grade Again or Hard and re-anchor on NICe.

questions.q: From memory: what is a needs analysis and what does it set out to do?
keyPoints: It is a questioning exercise that clarifies and defines the design task before designing begins.
It asks about the situation/context, the type of need, the target market and their demographics, what the solution must do, and the gap in existing products.
It confirms the need is genuine (via market research) and identifies any gap or niche.
Its answers tell you what the project must do to meet the target market.
questions.explanation: The two phrases markers reward are 'clarify and define the task' and 'confirm a genuine need / identify the gap'. If you got both, grade Good or Easy.

questions.q: Explain the purpose of a needs analysis. (3 marks)
questions.modelAnswer: A needs analysis is a questioning exercise that clarifies and defines the design task before designing begins. By systematically asking about the situation and its context, the type of need, the target market and their demographics, the required function of the solution, and how existing products fail to meet the need, the designer confirms that the need is genuine, identifies any gap or niche in the market, and establishes what the solution must achieve. This ensures the project addresses a real, well-understood need rather than an assumed one.

criteria.descriptor: States that a needs analysis clarifies and defines the design task through systematic questioning.
Explains that it confirms the need is genuine and identifies the gap or niche in existing products.
Explains that it establishes what the solution must do to meet the target market.

questions.explanation: The crux the marker wants is 'clarify and define the task' plus 'confirm a genuine need'. Naming the questions (situation, type of need, target market, required function, gap) secures full marks.

questions.q: Explain how a need or opportunity is identified and developed into a project proposal. (5 marks)
questions.modelAnswer: A designer first identifies a possible need — a consumer-driven problem — or an opportunity — a gap or niche in the market. This is then explored through a needs analysis, a questioning exercise that examines the situation, the target market and their demographics, the required function of the solution, and how existing products fail to meet the need, and it is confirmed as genuine through market research. From this analysis the designer formulates a project proposal that clearly outlines three things (NICe): the identified and explored need, supported by evidence; the areas of investigation to be researched; and measurable criteria to evaluate the project's success. In this way the proposal is derived from a properly analysed need rather than from an assumed solution.

criteria.descriptor: Distinguishes identifying a need (consumer-driven problem) from an opportunity (gap or niche), and explains exploration through a needs analysis confirmed by research.
Explains the formulation of the proposal, outlining all three NICe parts: explored need, areas of investigation, and measurable criteria.
Makes clear the proposal is derived from the analysed need rather than jumping to an assumed solution.

questions.explanation: The strong answer shows the process — analyse the need before naming the solution. A weak answer that jumps straight to 'I wanted to build X' misses the analysis and caps low.
